transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. I’m Dr. [Your Name]. What brings you in today?

Hi. I'm Santiago. Um... I guess I'm here because of some trouble I've been having lately. 

Late at night, mostly. I start picking at food, and... I don't know, it worries me a bit because I'll tell myself, 'That's enough, Santiago,' but... my hand just keeps going back for more. It's just... it feels like I don't get to make the decision anymore once I start. 

So... yeah. That's why I came in.
Can you describe what happens during these late-night eating episodes? Do you feel like you lose control once you start eating?

Yeah... I guess I do. Um... on some nights after work, I'll just be standing in the kitchen. I tell myself I'm just... cleaning up the leftovers, you know? But then I end up going through... I don't know, several tamales... a big bowl of pozole... tortillas, and whatever rice or beans are still sitting there. It just kind of... happens.
After these episodes, do you ever try to compensate for the food you’ve eaten, like making yourself vomit, using laxatives, or exercising a lot more than usual?
No... no, I don't do any of that. I just... go to sleep, mostly. I mean, I feel bad about it, but... I don't try to get rid of it or anything.
When you're having one of these late-night eating episodes, do you find yourself eating much more quickly than you normally would?

Yeah... I guess I do. Um... I eat it pretty fast. Not like... not like when I'm sitting down with the family. It's more like I'm just... trying to get it done before anyone wakes up. I don't think I'm even really tasting it.
Do you usually start eating these late-night meals because you feel physically hungry, or does it happen even when you're not really hungry?
I guess... not really. I mean, I usually eat dinner with my family earlier. So... I'm not really hungry when I do it. I just... find myself back at the fridge later on.
Do you usually eat alone during these late-night episodes because you're embarrassed about how much you're eating?
Yeah... I guess so. I just... I don't really want anyone seeing how much I'm putting away. So I just wait until my aunt and the rest of the house are asleep... try to keep it quiet in the kitchen.
After these late-night eating episodes, do you feel guilty, upset with yourself, or emotionally distressed about what you've eaten?
Yeah... I do. Um... I just feel bad about it. I don't know. It's just... I wish I didn't do it.
During these late-night eating episodes, do you feel like you can't stop eating or control how much you're eating once you start?

Yeah... um, I guess so. It's just... once I start picking at things, I try to stop. I tell myself that is enough, Santiago. But... I don't know. My hand just keeps going back. It feels like... like I don't really get to make the decision anymore.
Do these late-night eating episodes happen while you're fully awake, or do you usually eat like this after waking up in the middle of the night?
Um... I'm awake. I just... I stay up late, watching TV or whatever. I don't go to sleep and wake up to do it. Just... I'm already awake.

latest_inference.note: The patient confirms that the late-night eating episodes occur while fully awake and are characterized by a sense of loss of control once eating begins, meeting criteria for binge eating disorder. There is no evidence of compensatory behaviors, which rules out bulimia nervosa (F51.3).
